headline: German giant wind turbine taller than Eiffel Tower transforms renewable energy
meta_description: A 365-meter wind turbine in eastern Germany promises to double electricity output by harnessing stronger winds at greater heights, marking a shift in renewable…
summary_short: Germany's new 365-meter wind turbine—taller than the Eiffel Tower—can produce twice as much electricity as conventional turbines by reaching stronger, more consistent wi…
body:
A colossal wind turbine rising 365 meters above the German landscape near Schipkau is poised to transform how engineers think about renewable energy production. Built by Gicon, a Dresden-based engineering company, the prototype reaches higher than the Eiffel Tower's 330 meters and approaches the height of Berlin's television tower at 368 meters. The key innovation is its 300-meter hub height—the center point of the rotating blades—which allows it to access winds that are both stronger and more reliable than those found at conventional turbine heights, typically below 200 meters. According to Gicon's chief executive Jochen Grossmann, this elevation advantage could more than double electricity generation compared to existing facilities, while enabling power production throughout more of the year.

The turbine's arrival is particularly significant for Lusatia, a region in southeastern Germany that once depended on lignite mining and is now transitioning toward renewable energy. Set to be inaugurated in mid-November, the prototype serves as a proof-of-concept for larger-scale deployment. Gicon plans to use findings from this structure to develop wind farms containing three to five extra-tall turbines, potentially paving the way for mass production.

Beyond raw energy output, the design addresses a persistent challenge: the scarcity of suitable land. Grossmann envisions "two-story" wind farms that combine shorter and taller turbines on existing sites, maximizing space efficiency. Germany's commitment to renewables is clear—wind alone provided 29.4% of the nation's energy in the first half of 2026, with renewables overall reaching 59.1% of production. As Germany phases out coal by 2038, innovations like this towering turbine offer a tangible path toward meeting ambitious climate goals.
quick_facts: 365 meters tall—taller than the Eiffel Tower at 330 meters
Built in Schipkau, Lusatia, eastern Germany by Gicon company
Can produce more than double the electricity of conventional turbines
Wind energy provided 29.4% of German electricity in first half of 2026
